title: Scattering-Induced Magnon Layer-Hall Transport beyond Band Geometry
authors: Zhiping Xue, Zhoujian Sun, Xiyin Ye, Lei Zhang, Tao Yu
abstract: The layer Hall effect has been exclusively attributed to layer-locked Berry curvature, posing a fundamental barrier to its realization in conventional magnets. Here we report a fundamentally distinct layer Hall effect for bosonic excitations, i.e., magnons, which originates solely from non-reciprocal dipolar scattering at heterointerfaces, thereby decoupling the phenomenon from geometric-phase mechanisms. Using a microscopic scattering theory, we demonstrate that a longitudinal temperature gradient drives opposite transverse thermal Hall currents in a nanowire atop a magnetic film, with the direction fully reconfigurable by the applied magnetic field. The effect yields a significant Hall angle of $\sim 6^{\circ}$ in conventional magnetic heterostructures, eliminating the need for topological engineering. Our findings establish a scattering-driven paradigm for layer Hall effect, extendable to ferrons and polar phonons, and predict a Hall response that is readily detectable in conventional magnetic heterostructures.
summary: This work introduces a novel, scattering-driven mechanism for the layer Hall effect in magnons, bypassing the need for topological band structures. By analyzing a nanowire on a magnetic film, the authors show that non-reciprocal dipolar scattering under a temperature gradient generates measurable transverse thermal Hall currents. This provides a robust, field-tunable pathway for realizing this effect in conventional magnetic materials.
main_problem: To establish a fundamentally distinct mechanism for the layer Hall effect (LHE) in bosonic excitations, specifically magnons, that is driven by non-reciprocal dipolar scattering rather than geometric Berry curvature effects.
main_result: The study predicts a magnon LHE where a longitudinal temperature gradient drives opposite transverse thermal Hall currents, yielding a sizable Hall angle ($\sim 6^\circ$) in conventional magnetic heterostructures.
method: The authors employ a microscopic scattering theory approach, deriving hybridization coefficients and analyzing the resulting magnon current densities under a temperature gradient.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a hybrid chiral architecture: a magnetic nanowire placed atop a magnetic film, interacting via an interlayer dipolar coupling. The analysis focuses on the magnon excitations in this coupled system.

main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the ballistic regime (micrometer length scales) and attributes the effect to the non-reciprocity of the dipolar coupling, thereby bypassing the need for topological engineering.

paper_structure: The paper builds from identifying the limitations of Berry curvature mechanisms to developing a scattering-theory framework based on non-reciprocal dipolar coupling, calculating the resulting transverse currents, and demonstrating the tunability and magnitude of the effect.
why_interesting: While the primary focus is condensed matter magnetism, the development of a scattering-theory approach to engineer directional transport (thermal/spin currents) based on symmetry breaking (non-reciprocity) is highly relevant to open quantum systems and engineered quantum transport phenomena.

The magnetization of the film (nanowire) is tilted by an angle θ (˜θ) relative to the wire ˆz-axis. The film is sandwiched between two thermal reservoirs at temperatures TL and TR, establishing a longitudinal temperature gradient ∇T ∥ˆy.
